hero.title: File:Maevarano Formation polypterid (spiracular bone).gif
hero.artist: Murray, Alison M.; Brinkman, Donald B.; Gottfried, Michael D.; Krause, David W.
hero.credit: Murray, Alison M.; Brinkman, Donald B.; Gottfried, Michael D.; Krause, David W. (11 March 2026). "Late Cretaceous bichirs from Madagascar provide the first documentation of Polypteriformes (Actinopterygii, Cladistia) in Eastern Gondwana". Cretaceous Research 106370. doi:10.1016/j.cretres.2026.106370.
hero.description: Fossil bone identified as coming from the spiracular series from the Maevarano Formation, Madagascar, assigned to Polypteridae compared to the extant polypterid Polypterus endlicherii (UAMZ uncatalogued).Scale bars equal 5 mm.

gallery.title: File:Araripesuchus wegeneri.jpg
gallery.credit: Fig. 46C in Sereno PC, Larsson HCE (2009) Cretaceous Crocodyliforms from the Sahara. ZooKeys 28: 1–143. doi:10.3897/zookeys.28.325
gallery.description: Life restoration of Araripesuchus wegeneri.Adult (~81 cm) with proportions based on an adult skeleton (MNN GAD21), in which forelimb and hind limb comprise 50% and 75%, respectively, of trunk length.
categories: Open Access File of the Day

gallery.title: File:Simosuchus.jpg
gallery.description:
Life restoration of Simosuchus clarki.
Based on skeletal and restoration in "Overview of the discovery, distribution, and geological context of Simosuchus clarki (Crocodyliformes: Notosuchia) from the Late Cretaceous of Madagascar" by David W. Krause, Joseph J.W. Sertich, Raymond R. Rogers, Sophia C. Kast, Armand H. Rasoamiaramanana, and Gregory A. Buckley (Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology 30 (sp1): 4-12).
